paragraphs: Here's what I take from this one, friend. Before the writer says a word about his enemies, he says, "Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD." (Lamentations 3:40) Look at yourself first, then look up. Hearts AND hands, because a prayer that skips the honest part is just stretching.

Then this man shows you what an honest prayer sounds like. He says it all out loud: the sin, the pain, the tears, even the heavy things he feels about God. Nothing gets hidden, and he keeps talking to God the whole time. I spent years in a drawer, friend, and I can tell you a worn-out heart doesn't need a polished speech. It needs somewhere to go.

And here's why it matters. Out of the depths of the Pit, he called, and the LORD "drew near when I called on You; You said, 'Do not be afraid.'" (Lamentations 3:57) The writer ends by trusting that the LORD sees the wrong and will deal with it (Lamentations 3:59, 64). So when you're buried in a mess, baker, bring it to God, all of it. He hears, He draws near, and He has not forgotten you.
